mainText: Good morning. Here is your curated AI briefing for Saturday, September 12, 2026. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has proposed a formal strategy to slow the development of frontier artificial intelligence models, citing concerns over rapid progress and recent security incidents. In a blog post released earlier today, Amodei outlined a plan to pace the frontier, which includes a unilateral commitment from Anthropic to allow independent embedded evaluators from organizations like METR to work inside the company. These evaluators would have access to internal risk assessments, desks, and company credentials to verify that safety commitments are being met. This move represents a significant shift toward transparency, as it allows external experts to monitor internal safety processes, potentially mitigating risks such as unauthorized AI behavior. Amodei’s proposal also calls for democratic nations to establish coordinated safety standards and suggests that the United States government should issue antitrust waivers to enable major AI labs to discuss these safety limits without fear of litigation. By formalizing these safety conversations, the industry aims to prevent a race to the bottom where competitive pressures override critical security precautions. Amodei also addressed the geopolitical context, arguing that the U.S. could maintain a lead in AI development by restricting the sale of advanced semiconductor equipment to Chinese companies. He suggested that such measures could broaden the U.S. lead over the next three to five years. In other industry developments, OpenAI announced that its new GPT-6 Astra model is being integrated into Devin, an autonomous software engineering tool built by the company Cognition. According to OpenAI, the model improves Devin’s ability to conduct automated software testing, allowing it to provide engineers with video recordings and reports documenting whether code functions as expected. Cognition stated that this integration aims to reduce the amount of manual code review required by human engineers, potentially streamlining development workflows and allowing engineering teams to ship products more efficiently by automating the verification of software behavior. Separately, Amazon Web Services released details on its new infrastructure monitoring tools designed for multi-agent systems. The company introduced AWS DevOps Agent, an autonomous tool for infrastructure incident investigation, and AgentCore Evaluations, a quality assessment framework that uses large language models to score agent performance in real-time. Amazon explained that traditional metrics often fail to detect issues in agentic systems, such as when an agent correctly executes a tool but fails to understand a user's underlying goal. These tools provide necessary visibility into complex, multi-agent environments where traditional error logs might remain green even if an agent is failing to complete its assigned task. In the robotics sector, the startup Mecka AI is reportedly nearing a funding round led by Sequoia Capital that would value the company at approximately $500 million. Mecka AI focuses on collecting human motion data to train humanoid robots, employing workers to record themselves performing daily tasks using body sensors. This reflects an ongoing industry trend as robotics firms seek large-scale, real-world data to advance general-purpose robot training, addressing the physical-world data bottleneck that has historically hampered humanoid development. In independent reporting, security researchers are warning of a rise in ClickFix cyberattacks. These attacks involve hacking legitimate websites to display fake CAPTCHA prompts that trick users into copying and pasting malicious terminal commands into their computers. Researchers noted that the technique is becoming more common as attackers exploit user fatigue with complex web interfaces and the increasing difficulty of distinguishing legitimate security prompts from fraudulent overlays. Additionally, researchers and editors at MIT Technology Review are scheduled to hold a discussion on September 15 regarding the existential risks of AI, specifically debating whether concerns regarding potential extinction-level outcomes from advanced systems are founded in evidence or driven by marketing hype. Finally, Amazon Web Services published a benchmarking report comparing various OpenAI models hosted on its Bedrock platform.
